findings.title: Upgrade test (T100420-10 / exit-contract rule 4) never opens a previous-schema database; the old-index drop and the v10 to v11 migration are untested
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/triple_open_uniq_tests.rs:341-377 `sqlite_existing_db_gains_unique_index_on_reopen` creates the database with the CURRENT schema (`SqliteStore::open`) and then only runs `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS triples_open_uniq`; crates/clio-store/src/pg_triple_open_uniq_tests.rs:192-230 `pg_existing_db_gains_unique_index_on_reopen` does the same. Neither test creates `triples_bank_id_subject_predicate_open_both_inx`, seeds schema_version '10', or otherwise materializes the previous schema shape. `grep -rn triples_bank_id_subject_predicate_open_both_inx` outside roadmap text finds the name only at sql/001_core.sql:259 (the DROP) and crates/clio-store/src/migrate.rs:121 (the SQL-text assertion); no test materializes the old index so the DROP has something to remove, and no test opens a real v10 database that must come up at v11.
findings.requirement_ref: roadmap/phase-100420 section 5 Task 3 Required Changes 5; section 8 T100420-10; section 12 Pre-existing-Data Compatibility Policy rule 4 ("At least one test opens a database created with the previous schema")
findings.recommendation: Add one test per backend that builds a v10-shaped database (old non-unique `triples_bank_id_subject_predicate_open_both_inx` present, `schema_version` '10', no `triples_open_uniq`), opens the store, and asserts: the old index is gone, `triples_open_uniq` exists and rejects a raw duplicate insert, and `schema_version` reads '11'.

findings.title: New subject-immutability guard assumes a non-NULL stored subject_id: a NULL row panics the Postgres update and returns a generic driver error on SQLite
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs:53-61 (SQLite) reads the stored subject into `String` (`|r| r.get(0)`); a NULL raises rusqlite InvalidColumnType which `.am("subject lookup")` maps to a generic `Internal` error (crates/clio-store/src/migrate.rs:18-20). crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs:135-141 (Postgres) calls `row.get(0)` inside `.map(...)`, and postgres::Row::get panics on a conversion failure. sql/001_core.sql:130 declares `subject_id text,` (nullable) and crates/clio-store/src/schema_converge.rs only adds the correction-lineage columns, so a legacy or hand-written row with NULL subject_id hits this path; every current write path supplies a non-empty subject, so reachability is limited to data written outside the current API.
findings.recommendation: Read the stored subject as `Option<String>` on both backends and handle NULL explicitly (return the named error, or allow the update when the caller supplies a subject), instead of a generic driver error on SQLite and a panic on Postgres.

findings.title: F-05 remediation is partial: the ungated correction primitive can still re-point an item to another subject (DEK/erasure-domain move)
findings.evidence: The F-05 fix rejects subject changes only in `update_memory_item_*_tx` (crates/clio-store/src/item_update.rs:62-64 and :148-150). The correction primitive still takes a caller-built `MemoryItem` (crates/clio-store/src/audit_model.rs:35-42, `pub new_item: MemoryItem`), seals it under `new_item.subject_id` (crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_correct.rs:48-53; postgres_correct.rs parity) and inserts that subject (sqlite_correct.rs:104-140) without comparing it to the prior row's subject. The compliance facade builds `new_item` from the prior item (crates/clio-compliance/src/correct.rs:177 `build_corrected_item(&prior, ...)`), so exposed tool paths are safe; direct library callers can still move a record out of its subject's erasure scope.
findings.requirement_ref: FR-19 / requirement.md section 7.4 (erasure scope by subject); phase-100420 Task 2 finding F-05 disposition
findings.recommendation: Add the same stored-subject comparison to `correct_item_impl` and its Postgres twin (reject `spec.new_item.subject_id != prior.subject_id` with the named error), or document the correction move as an explicit, audited operation.

findings.title: New constraint tests drop a live index on the shared public schema, against the phase's "No destructive DDL on public" control
findings.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/pg_triple_open_uniq_tests.rs:214 and :256 run `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS triples_open_uniq` against the shared Compose database (`DATABASE_URL`, public schema), and :283-287 deletes rows; roadmap/phase-100420 section 7 Required Controls state "No destructive DDL on `public`" and prefer a private schema per coverage.md section 4.4. The serialization lock is a process-wide mutex (crates/clio-store/src/pg_lock.rs:16-27) and the index is restored only by the next `PostgresStore::open` (crates/clio-store/src/postgres.rs:63-64), so a process dying between the drop and the reopen leaves the shared database without the DB backstop until some later store open. The repo already has the private-schema pattern for DDL cases: crates/clio-store/src/pg_assoc_edge_tests.rs:156-178 creates a temporary schema and sets search_path.
findings.recommendation: Run the drop/reopen and legacy-duplicate Postgres cases in a private temporary schema (CREATE SCHEMA + search_path + schema bootstrap) as pg_assoc_edge_tests does, or guarantee index restoration in a drop guard so a panic cannot leave the shared schema without the constraint.
